title: Battle of the bands in Flint with an old rival
summary: Roy led the band, and the carnival pianist who had mocked him challenged him; the band beat him with classical arrangements and then a screamer.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: I ended up with the band... Last gig we played was a gig that I got in Flint, Michigan. And you know what's funny? The guy that used to hate me on that carnival, you know, the piano player who said I'd never make it, he came to Flint, and it was... (?) like that is where I got the gig. Even though I was in charge of the band, see. But he come up and he said, "Are you still trying to play trumpet?" And I said, "Well, I still hold it." And he said (he was in a band out of Detroit), "Man, I feel sorry for you, because we're gonna wash you away tonight." And I said, "Well, okay."

And at least it played a... What would you call it? The strategy in battling with bands, you know, especially when the band don't know what you're putting down. We had a lot of those semi-classical arrangements, "Ein Liebestraum" and things like that. We played those, man, and these cats got up there, and the bass player rode the bass, you know... Oh, they was goin' through their thing, you know. So we just kept on playing some nice fancy music; we had some nice things, you know. Then, about the middle of the night,

what we used to call the belly of the night, we opened up with one of our screamers. And I could see this cat's mouth saying... Heh-heh-heh. He couldn't believe it! Then they sounded like three pieces. Oh man. And then we just kept on going. And the cat said... At the end he said, "I always knew you'd make it." I said, "Yeah? Thanks."
I'm sure he just... You know, that's why I would never put a cat down when he's trying to come up and make it, you know. Because you never know what position he's going to be in.
